findings.refutation: The g20-fixture-corpus.v6 findings did not land at g20-fixture-corpus.v8. They landed at g20-fixture-corpus.v7, and four independent sources say so. Frozen g20-fixture-corpus.v7 $.authorityClaim reads 'g20-fixture-corpus.v7 lands g20-fixture-corpus.v6 Stage A Claude CLAUDE-G20FX-V6-M-1 through CLAUDE-G20FX-V6-M-5 and CLAUDE-G20FX-V6-S-1 and CLAUDE-G20FX-V6-S-2, and the unlabeled Codex Stage A MUST-FIX and SHOULD-FIX of the same two classes.' The frozen g20-fixture-corpus.v7 Claude review confirms it landed against live bytes: 'All five Claude MUST-FIX, both Claude SHOULD-FIX and both unlabelled Codex findings are repaired against live bytes.' The predecessor's own copy of this very clause read 'Findings land at g20-fixture-corpus.v7.', which was true. And the subject's own $.authorityClaim contradicts the clause directly: it enumerates what this candidate lands, and the list is exactly one item - 'g20-fixture-corpus.v8 lands g20-fixture-corpus.v7 Stage A Claude CLAUDE-G20FX-V7-M-1.' - with no mention of any V6 finding. The subject therefore asserts in one clause that the seven V6 findings land at v8, and in another that v8 lands only CLAUDE-G20FX-V7-M-1. Both cannot be true, and live bytes settle it against the clause under review. The token was carried by the same mechanical v7->v8 sweep that correctly advanced roughly thirty self-referential speaker tokens elsewhere; here the token was not a self-reference but a record of which artifact performed a completed historical repair, and it had to stay fixed at v7.
findings.whyItIsAFinding: This is the same class the successor was dispatched to repair - a current-standing clause in the artifact's own voice that live bytes refute - reintroduced by the repair pass at a site no finding asked to be rewritten. It is worse than a stale clause because the correct value is not recoverable from within the artifact: after this edit g20-fixture-corpus.v8 states nowhere that the V6 findings landed at v7. basedOn.predecessorV7.role records only that v7 was REJECT on CLAUDE-G20FX-V7-M-1 with Codex ACCEPT 0/0; it does not record what v7 landed. A later remasurement reading v8 to find where the seven V6 findings were repaired is routed to v8 itself, which did not repair them, with nothing in the file to correct it beyond a contradiction it must first detect and then adjudicate. I grade it MUST-FIX rather than SHOULD-FIX by the same reasoning the v7 review used for its own M-1 and the v6 review used to separate M-5 from S-2: a defect is SHOULD-FIX when sibling clauses carry the right answer and MUST-FIX when they do not. Here the siblings carry a contradiction, not the answer.

findings.claim: "...with file 08, g20 leftover-join.v9, g20 leftover-join.v6, sdk leftover-join.v6, occupancy v2, the ten fixtures/g20.v2/ files, frozen g20-fixture-corpus.v1 through g20-fixture-corpus.v6, and g20-fixture-corpus.v8 unmoved, remasure before recording."
findings.refutation: The custody set omits g20-fixture-corpus.v7. The clause names a frozen range v1 through v6 and then the subject v8; v7 falls in neither slot and appears nowhere else in the clause. v7 is a frozen predecessor by this artifact's own account: basedOn.predecessorV7 pins it with a verified digest, recordedInputs pins it and its two reviews, authorityClaim says 'Frozen g20-fixture-corpus.v7 stays unmoved and unrecorded.', purpose says 'Frozen g20-fixture-corpus.v7 stays unmoved.', and doesNot[42] says 'Does not record g20-fixture-corpus.v7 as current.' The artifact thus requires v7 to stay unmoved in four places while excluding it from the one clause that defines which movements trigger remasurement before recording. The predecessor's copy of this clause read 'frozen g20-fixture-corpus.v1 through g20-fixture-corpus.v6, and g20-fixture-corpus.v7 unmoved', which was complete at v7 because the range ended exactly one below the subject. The v7->v8 sweep advanced the subject token 7->8 and left the range at v6, evicting v7 from the sentence.
findings.whyItIsAFinding: This is a regression of a SHOULD-FIX already raised and already landed in this lineage, at the identical site and by the identical mechanism. CLAUDE-G20FX-V6-S-1 was raised against $.remeasurementClause when it read 'frozen g20-fixture-corpus.v1 through g20-fixture-corpus.v4, and g20-fixture-corpus.v6 unmoved' - v5 had been evicted the same way, by the subject slot advancing while the range stood still - and its repairShape was 'Extend the range to frozen g20-fixture-corpus.v1 through g20-fixture-corpus.v5'. The v7 author landed that repair by widening the range to v6. The v8 author reopened the gap one version later. The consequence is operational, not cosmetic: the clause is this artifact's own trigger condition for remasuring before a D-000 recording, so as written a later recording could pin g20-fixture-corpus.v8 while g20-fixture-corpus.v7 had silently moved, and the artifact's own remasurement condition would not fire on it. I grade it SHOULD-FIX rather than MUST-FIX to match the grade the identical defect carried at CLAUDE-G20FX-V6-S-1, and because the correct answer is recoverable: four sibling clauses state that v7 must stay unmoved, so a careful later reader can reconstruct the intended custody set.
findings.repairShape: Extend the range by one, exactly as the v6 finding's repair was applied at v7: '...the ten fixtures/g20.v2/ files, frozen g20-fixture-corpus.v1 through g20-fixture-corpus.v7, and g20-fixture-corpus.v8 unmoved, remasure before recording.' Nothing else in the clause needs to move; g20 leftover-join.v9 is already named, both leftover-join tokens are already lineage-qualified, and the remaining sentences verify. Applying the same rule at every future successor - the frozen range ends at the subject's version minus one - closes this defect class permanently rather than one version at a time.
